assertions.description: PublicKeyCredential.getClientCapabilities is a function — the feature-detection surface for passive mode.
getClientCapabilities() reports conditionalPassiveGet: true (Chromium's prototype name ambientGet is accepted as the same capability).
CredentialRequestOptions.uiMode is a recognised member: an invalid value makes navigator.credentials.get() reject with TypeError instead of being ignored.
assertions.test: navigator.credentials.get({ mediation: 'conditional', uiMode: 'not-a-ui-mode', publicKey: { challenge: new Uint8Array(32) } }).then(() => false, e => e.name === 'TypeError')

assertions.description: A conditional request with uiMode 'passive' but no publicKey (passwords only) rejects with NotSupportedError — conditional mediation is a WebAuthn request.
assertions.test: navigator.credentials.get({ mediation: 'conditional', uiMode: 'passive', password: true }).then(() => false, e => e.name === 'NotSupportedError')

assertions.description: With passive mode enabled, uiMode 'passive' combined with a federated credential request rejects with NotSupportedError, while the same request without uiMode does not reject that way (the passive branch really runs).
assertions.test: (async () => { const run = async (o) => { const c = new AbortController(); const p = navigator.credentials.get({ ...o, signal: c.signal }).then(() => 'resolved', e => e.name + ':' + e.message); const r = await Promise.race([p, new Promise(res => setTimeout(() => res('pending'), 700))]); c.abort(); await p; return r; }; const base = () => ({ mediation: 'conditional', publicKey: { challenge: crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32)) }, federated: { providers: ['https://idp.example'] } }); const control = await run(base()); const passive = await run({ ...base(), uiMode: 'passive' }); return passive.startsWith('NotSupportedError') && passive !== control; })()

assertions.description: A pending passive request is cancellable: aborting its AbortSignal rejects the promise with AbortError (or it had already settled without resolving to a fake credential).
assertions.test: (async () => { const c = new AbortController(); const p = navigator.credentials.get({ mediation: 'conditional', uiMode: 'passive', publicKey: { challenge: crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32)), allowCredentials: [{ type: 'public-key', id: crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(32)) }] }, signal: c.signal }).then(() => 'resolved', e => e.name); const early = await Promise.race([p, new Promise(r => setTimeout(() => r(null), 300))]); c.abort(); const r = early ?? await p; return early === null ? r === 'AbortError' : r !== 'resolved'; })()

assertions.description: With a discoverable credential for the RP, a passive request immediately shows a non-modal, ignorable prompt (no sign-in form needed), and choosing an account resolves the promise with a PublicKeyCredential.
assertions.test: Requires chrome://flags/#web-authentication-ambient-signin (or --enable-features=WebAuthenticationAmbientSignin), a real passkey for the origin and a human choosing it in browser UI. Observe via /v157/web-authentication-conditional-ui-passive-mode/passive-sign-in-request/.

assertions.description: With no eligible credentials, a passive request shows no UI and its promise never settles on its own (no signal to the site that the user lacks an account).
assertions.test: Requires the flag and a profile with no passkey for the origin; the request must stay pending until aborted. Observe the pending timer on /v157/web-authentication-conditional-ui-passive-mode/passive-sign-in-request/.

assertions.description: One passive conditional request also feeds webauthn autofill: after the passive prompt is ignored, focusing an autocomplete="username webauthn" field offers the same credentials and selecting one settles the same promise.
assertions.test: Requires the flag, a passkey for the origin and human interaction with browser autofill UI. Observe via /v157/web-authentication-conditional-ui-passive-mode/passive-plus-autofill/.
